summary: A2UI is a real external protocol — a2ui-project/a2ui, 16,230 stars, pushed today, Apache-2.0, with an official React renderer (@a2ui/react@0.10.2) and independent ports to .NET, Swift, Android, and React Native. Our schema is artifact-refiner.dev-namespaced, cites no upstream, and diverges structurally at every level: `type` vs `component` discriminator, single tree vs envelope stream (createSurface/updateComponents/updateDataModel/...), bindings map vs DynamicString + updateDataModel, open ^[A-Z] pattern vs catalog.json. Specs our refiner validates are not A2UI protocol documents.

blocking_escalation.title: Align our A2UI to the real protocol, rename the local dialect, or support both?
blocking_escalation.why_not_decided_here: It changes the meaning of a shipped domain (direct:a2ui, PR #1) and invalidates published examples. The right answer turns on whether the refiner is meant to produce artifacts other systems consume — a product question, not a research one. Deciding it silently inside a research artifact would bury a breaking change.
options: Align to upstream v1.0 — interoperable, @a2ui/react renders for free; breaking, invalidates both examples, refiner reworked to the envelope model
Keep the dialect and rename it — no breaking change, phase stays small; but the name is taken, permanently non-interoperable, future readers will assume conformance
Support both — migration path at roughly double the surface; not recommended
blocking_escalation.analyze_observation: Option 2 is cheapest today and most expensive later; alignment cost grows with every spec authored against the dialect.

correction_to_prior_stage.claim: A2UI is a static document with no transport; 'arguably no store at all'
correction_to_prior_stage.evidence: Upstream: 'The A2UI Protocol facilitates the dynamic rendering of user interfaces by streaming JSON objects from an agent to a renderer... allowing for progressive rendering.' Transports are JSON Lines streams.
correction_to_prior_stage.impact: F-1 argued the phase-7 substrate does NOT transfer because A2UI has no stream. The opposite holds — A2UI is streaming-first, so the store/subscription/accumulation architecture transfers MORE than assess concluded. Root cause: I read our own schema and inferred the protocol from it.

decisions: Q2 CLOSED unconditionally: React either way. Under alignment @a2ui/react is the official renderer; under the dialect the scaffolder substrate is React and the Lit renderer has never rendered a conformant spec, so 'keep Lit' means rewrite-in-Lit, which is strictly worse.
ADOPT @a2ui/react@0.10.2 (Apache-2.0) conditional on G-8 aligning — eliminates G-1, G-4, and most of G-2. Pin exact (pre-1.0).
REJECT the existing Lit renderer as a basis; its preview shell (brand CSS, layout, screenshot harness) is salvageable, the ~30-line switch is not.
@a2ui/web_core@0.10.6 named as the framework-agnostic seam — arrives transitively for a React host, publishes more recently than the React wrapper.
warnings_from_adversarial_review: DROPPED GAPS — third occurrence of the same error. An earlier draft collapsed G-1..G-4 into one row and omitted G-5/G-6/G-7 entirely. All eight gaps now carry explicit verdicts. Plan should verify every carried gap has a disposition before proceeding; this failure mode has now appeared in phase-7 analyze (3 CRITICALs) and here.

DECLINED CRITICAL: the judge held that leaving G-8 unresolved denies plan a determinate target. Declined with reasoning — G-8 is an owner decision about a shipped domain, and the phase is otherwise decidable (Q2 closed, all gaps verdicted, both branches estimated). Plan can be written the moment G-8 is answered.
@a2ui/react risks: pre-1.0; npm publish lags the repo by ~6 weeks (repo 2026-08-28, package 2026-07-17); `@a2ui/markdown-it` declared as `*`, an unbounded range in a published dependency.
Upstream specification/v1_0/** paths are external (Context7 /a2ui-project/a2ui), not in this repo. Re-verify via Context7 rather than expecting them to resolve locally.
G-7 (five unpinned unpkg @latest CDN loads) stands either way and makes any browser-DOM verification flaky until pinned.

estimate.keep_dialect_finish_preview: 1 session, 4-6 changes — ships a permanently non-interoperable artifact type
estimate.align_upstream_adopt_renderer: 2-3 sessions, 8-12 changes — most of it reworking schema/normalizer/examples, not writing a renderer
estimate.note: The assess estimate assumed a hand-written renderer was the work. Under alignment it is not — the renderer is adopted and the work moves to the refiner and examples.

next_stage_blocked_on: G-8 — spec cannot define changes until the document model is chosen.
